audit.whatIsWrong: The content layer names Heimerdinger's BASIC abilities using their UPGRADE!!!-empowered forms, in every stage of the lane. "H-28G Apex Turret" is used for the level-1 turrets (early, wants.you[0], wants.foe[0]) and "CH-3X Lightning Grenade" is used for the level-4 grenade (mid, whys[2], wants.foe[2]).
audit.why: H-28G Apex Turret and CH-3X Lightning Grenade only exist while UPGRADE!!! (R) is buffering the next cast — they are the R+Q and R+E forms. The abilities Tahm Kench actually faces from level 1 to 5 are H-28 G Evolution Turret (Q) and CH-2 Electron Storm Grenade (E). A player reading this is being taught the wrong names for the only two abilities that decide the lane, and would also reasonably conclude the ultimate-tier versions are up at level 1.
audit.corrected: Use H-28 G Evolution Turret and CH-2 Electron Storm Grenade for the basic abilities; reserve the Apex/CH-3X names for the level-6 UPGRADE!!! discussion only.
sources: champ-data/_kits/heimerdinger.json — Q 'H-28 G Evolution Turret', E 'CH-2 Electron Storm Grenade', R 'UPGRADE!!!' ('causes his next spell to have increased effects')

audit.whatIsWrong: The level-6 advice is built entirely on "Abyssal Voyage" — spikes[2] ("your Abyssal Voyage repositioning is irrelevant to lane; neither your global nor your stun resolves the zone"), mid ("your Abyssal Voyage is not yet available to threaten a roam" and "At 6 your Abyssal Voyage gives you a global signal") and whys[4] ("Abyssal Voyage is global utility, not a lane resolver").
audit.why: Abyssal Voyage is the pre-2021-rework Tahm Kench ultimate. It is not in the live kit. Tahm Kench has NO global ability, so the advice to 'threaten a roam', 'give a global signal' and 'impact other lanes' at 6 describes a champion that does not exist. Live level 6 is Devour, and the constraint that actually matters is that Devour cannot be used on an enemy champion until An Acquired Taste is at three stacks — which is precisely the thing Heimerdinger's zone prevents.
audit.corrected: Level 6 is Devour, gated behind three An Acquired Taste stacks on the target. It is a lockdown tool, not an escape and not a global, and it does not answer an unmanned turret zone.
sources: champ-data/_kits/tahmkench.json — R is Devour; P: 'At three stacks, he can use Devour on an enemy champion'; no global ability in kit

audit.whatIsWrong: wants.foe[2] claims Heimerdinger's grenade will "reset your stack count to zero".
audit.why: Nothing in Heimerdinger's kit removes An Acquired Taste stacks, and nothing in Tahm Kench's kit says stacks are lost to being stunned. Stacks are consumed only when the Q stun fires. This is an invented mechanic, and it is the kind a player would act on — they would stop trying to hold a partial stack count through a grenade, which is exactly the wrong lesson.
audit.corrected: The grenade's real function is to stun the commit before the third stack lands, not to wipe stacks already banked.
sources: champ-data/_kits/tahmkench.json — Q: 'If the champion already has 3 stacks... they are stunned and the stacks are consumed'; champ-data/_kits/heimerdinger.json — E has no stack-removal clause

audit.whatIsWrong: Both layers repeat "track CH-2 Grenade" / "engage only on CH-2 Grenade's cooldown" a dozen times without ever giving the cooldown, and the mid text asserts the grenade "range is longer than your Q" without numbers.
audit.why: CH-2 Electron Storm Grenade is a FLAT 11 seconds at every rank — it does not scale down, which is unusual and genuinely useful to know because the punish window never shrinks as the lane goes on. Its range is 970 against Tongue Lash's 900, so the range edge is only 70 units, not the gulf the text implies; the ability that really out-ranges Tahm Kench is Hextech Micro-Rockets at 1325. UPGRADE!!! is 100s at rank 1.
audit.corrected: State 11s flat and 970 vs 900 where the text tells the player to wait for the grenade.
sources: champ-data/_kits/heimerdinger.json — E cooldown '11', range 970; W range 1325; R cooldown 100/85/70. champ-data/_kits/tahmkench.json — Q range 900

audit.whatIsWrong: 43.96% over 298 games is Tahm Kench's WORST top-lane matchup in the entire 71-entry table (next worst is Yorick at 45.77%), yet it is rated TRICKY 7.5/10 — softer than Gwen (48.97%, HARD 8.5), Teemo (54.57%, HARD 8.5) and Cassiopeia (54.75%, HARD 8.5), all of which Tahm Kench either draws or wins.
audit.why: Whatever the scale is measuring, the single hardest lane by result sitting below three lanes Tahm Kench wins is not defensible.
audit.corrected: Should read HARD / 8.5/10. I deliberately did NOT propose this as an edit: 'TRICKY' -> 'HARD' is a 0.67 length ratio and would be auto-rejected, so changing diffRating alone would desync it from diff, breakdown.difficulty ('Overall difficulty: 7.5/10') and report 'Final Matchup Rating' ('Tricky matchup'). All four need to move together, by hand or by the applier.
sources: packet winRate 43.96 / games 298; CHAMP_FULL.tahmkench diff+diffRating across all 71 entries

audit.why: The 2-item flip is the right win condition and is well argued — Heimerdinger's poke is front-loaded and his zone is static, so Thick Skin's grey-health pool scaling with Heartsteel HP genuinely does outgrow it. Left alone apart from the ability names inside it.
sources: champ-data/_kits/tahmkench.json — E Thick Skin stores a percent of damage taken; champ-data/_kits/heimerdinger.json — no mobility, no reposition tool

edits.before: Levels 4 through 5 are the most punishing window of the lane — Heimerdinger has his full three-turret pattern, his CH-3X Lightning Grenade range is longer than your Q, and your Abyssal Voyage is not yet available to threaten a roam. Stay behind the wave, let minions tank turret shots, and fish for a single overextended turret he drops without body support: if you can destroy an isolated turret and step back before the grenade lands you deny him vision and zone control simultaneously. Never commit your Flash here; you need it for the level-6 repositioning threat or to escape a turret-into-grenade double stun. At 6 your Abyssal Voyage gives you a global signal — he has to respect your presence in river — but it does not win you this lane; use it to impact other lanes and come back to farm.
edits.after: Levels 4 through 5 are the most punishing window of the lane — Heimerdinger has his full three-turret pattern, his CH-2 Electron Storm Grenade reaches 970 against your Q's 900, and you have no ultimate yet. Stay behind the wave, let minions tank turret shots, and fish for a single overextended turret he drops without body support: if you can destroy an isolated turret and step back before the grenade lands you deny him vision and zone control simultaneously. Never commit your Flash here; you need it to escape a turret-into-grenade double stun. At 6 Devour is a lockdown, not an escape — it needs three An Acquired Taste stacks on him before it can be cast at all, so it does not resolve the zone; farm what you can and look for picks off the wave.

edits.before: You cannot brute-force through a full turret line at level 1 — Heimerdinger's H-28G Apex Turrets plus his own body mean two sources of damage hit you simultaneously the moment you step into stack range. Farm from the absolute tip of Tongue Lash, accept that you will lose some CS to turret denial, and use Thick Skin passively rather than forcing grey-health conversion early when his poke can immediately refill the grey bar. Your only real level-1 agency is threatening a Tongue Lash slow so he cannot freely walk his turrets onto your side of the wave.

edits.after: Heimerdinger's UPGRADE!!! turns Q into an H-28G Apex Turret or E into CH-3X Lightning Grenade on a 100s cooldown; your 6 is Devour, and it needs three stacks on him before it can be cast.

edits.after: Three turrets plus CH-2 Electron Storm Grenade at 970 range beat your reliable An Acquired Taste stacking distance — he denies the combo and punishes every approach.

edits.before: - Heimerdinger CH-2 Grenade: matchup-defining — His self-peel stun. Dodge it. Track it before every engage. - Your committal tool: never spend it on chip. - Your ultimate: the win condition — kill windows only.

notes: The "Abyssal Voyage" defect is far larger than this matchup: grep counts 62 occurrences in champ-data/content/tahmkench.js alone and 84 across 23 files in champ-data/. Abyssal Voyage was removed from Tahm Kench in the 2021 rework (live W is Abyssal Dive, live R is Devour), so every one of those lines is telling a player to use an ability that does not exist — and many of them, like this matchup's, hang the entire level-6 and late-game plan on it. The packet's suspectNames detector cannot catch this because it only scores near-miss spellings of names that DO exist in the kit. This needs a dedicated sweep across all owners, not just top lane. Second, unrelated: CHAMP_FULL.tahmkench.heimerdinger.phases[].side and MC_CONTENT_EXTRA heimerdinger.win disagree at six of seven stages (full has Tahm Kench favoured at 3, 4-5, first item and 2+ items; content has Skill/Skill at 4-5 and first item and Heimerdinger favoured at 3 and 4-5). In a lane Tahm Kench loses at 43.96% the full layer's version is the more suspect of the two. I did not propose side edits because the values are single words outside the +/-10% length band.
